findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS cron deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, whatever its method. Only this file increments retryCount today, so nothing is deleted wrongly yet. A future retry counter on email or WhatsApp reminders would have this cron delete them. Put `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` on that branch.

findings.title: Failing update inside catch aborts the whole batch; exhausted reminders are dropped silently
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block is not guarded. If it throws (for example a DB error), the exception leaves the loop. The remaining reminders are skipped and the handler rejects. Wrap it in its own try/catch, or increment the count outside the try block. Separately, a reminder whose retryCount passes 1 is deleted on the next run with no log. The SMS is lost without any trace, so log the give-up when it happens.

contracts.action: Increment retryCount on failed or null scheduleSMS, and delete reminders with retryCount > 1
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing deleteMany of past-due SMS reminders at the top of the same handler
contracts.before_after: Before: only past-due SMS reminders were deleted. After: reminders that failed twice are also deleted, so a persistently failing reminder is retried at most twice per cron run.
contracts.visible_effect: A reminder that fails twice is removed and the SMS is never sent. No user-visible signal.
contracts.failure_mode: If the update in the catch throws, the loop aborts. The retry loop is bounded by the retryCount cap of 2 runs, and each run is bounded by the number of reminders.

summary: The migration and schema change are fine. In the cron handler, the `retryCount > 1` delete branch is not limited to SMS reminders. The update in the catch block can abort the whole batch if it throws. Reminders that exhaust their retries are deleted with no log.
